specPoints.text: understand that variation within a species can be genetic, environmental, or a combination of both

primer.text: Why does one brother speak with a different accent, and why do siblings differ in blood group? This note sorts variation into its causes — genes through random fertilisation, environment during life, or both together — and introduces the discontinuous-versus-continuous split that tells you which cause dominates for a given trait.

lessons.title: The Three Cause Piles
lessons.opening: Variation means the differences between individuals of one species, and its causes sort into three piles: genetic differences inherited through random fertilisation, environmental pressures acting during life, or the two working together.
keyPoints: Variation is the differences between individuals of the same species.
Genetic causes run through the random fertilisation of gametes.
Environmental causes include climate, diet, accidents, culture and lifestyle.
Scarring, weight gain, spoken accent and a shaded plant's growth are taught examples.

low.restatement: Some differences are inherited, some are learned or suffered, some are both.
low.analogy: A card game where the deal is the genes and how you play is the environment.
low.examPointer: Learn the four environmental examples verbatim.

medium.restatement: Environment means anything outside the organism, so culture and lifestyle count alongside climate and diet.
medium.analogy: Everything beyond the skin counts as environment, including classrooms and kitchens.
medium.examPointer: Sort unfamiliar examples by asking whether genes could supply them.

check.stem: What is variation, as defined here?

options.text: Differences between individuals of the same species
options.explanation: Correct — this follows directly from the definition.
Within one species is the taught scope.
Mutation is one genetic source, not the definition.

options.text: Genetic, environmental, or a combination of both
options.explanation: Yes — the mechanism works exactly this way.

check.stem: Which example is environmental rather than genetic?

options.text: A scar left by an accident
options.explanation: Yes — the mechanism works exactly this way.

check.stem: How does a shaded plant growing taller to reach light illustrate environment?

options.text: Light availability during growth altered the height the genes allowed
options.explanation: Right — this is the account the lesson teaches.

options.text: Its genes changed in the shade
options.explanation: Genes stay fixed; the conditions changed.

check.stem: Why is spoken accent an environmental trait?

options.text: It is learned from the surrounding culture, not inherited
options.explanation: Right — this is the account the lesson teaches.
Blood group is unrelated to speech.
They vary precisely because culture varies.

check.stem: State the definition of variation and its causes.
check.modelAnswer: Variation is the differences between individuals of the same species, caused by genes, environmental factors, or both together.

check.stem: Give two environmental examples from the note.
check.modelAnswer: Scarring from an accident and weight gain from diet and inactivity.

check.stem: Explain why language counts as environmental variation.
check.modelAnswer: A person acquires the language and accent of their upbringing through exposure rather than inheritance, so the environment, not the genes, decides it.

check.stem: Two identical twins are raised in different countries and grow up speaking different languages. Classify this difference and justify your answer.
check.modelAnswer: The language difference is environmental, because the twins share their genes but acquired different speech through their different cultures.

lessons.title: Discontinuous Versus Continuous
lessons.opening: The two causes rarely work alone: discontinuous traits like blood group usually run on a single gene, while continuous traits like height blend polygenic genes with the environment, so genes set the potential and the surroundings decide how much of it develops.
keyPoints: Discontinuous variation is usually genetic alone and monogenic.
Blood group, tongue rolling and PTC tasting illustrate the discontinuous class.
Continuous variation mixes polygenic genes with environmental influence.
Tall parents pass on height genes, and diet then adjusts where inside that potential the child lands.
Genes decide what is inherited; the environment shapes how it develops.

low.restatement: Either-or traits come from single genes; spread-out traits mix genes with surroundings.
low.analogy: A light switch versus a dimmer slide controlled by two hands.
low.examPointer: Attach the right example to the right class: blood group versus height.

medium.restatement: The continuous case works because polygenic potential is a range, and the environment positions each individual inside it.
medium.analogy: Genes set the orchestra's range; the venue's acoustics tune the final sound.
medium.examPointer: Use the phrase genetic potential when explaining height.

options.text: Genetic variation alone, through a single gene
options.explanation: Correct — this matches the account taught above.
The taught rule assigns it to genes.
Accidents are environmental, not discontinuous causes.
Yes — the mechanism works exactly this way.
Skin colour spreads across a range.

check.stem: Why does height show the combined case?

options.text: Height genes set potential, while diet and lifestyle adjust the outcome
options.explanation: Right — the other options each misplace a concept.

options.text: Height has no genes at all

check.stem: What does polygenic inheritance contribute to continuous variation?

options.text: Several genes each add an effect, spreading the trait across a range
options.explanation: Right — this is the account the lesson teaches.
One gene gives classes, not ranges.

check.stem: A child of tall parents grows up short through poor diet. What does this show?

options.text: The environment limited the genetic potential for height
options.explanation: Correct — this follows directly from the definition.

options.text: The parents were not really tall

check.stem: Contrast discontinuous and continuous variation by cause.
check.modelAnswer: Discontinuous variation is usually genetic and monogenic, while continuous variation combines polygenic genes with environmental factors.
Blood group, the ability to roll the tongue, and PTC tasting.

check.stem: Explain why the same height genes can produce different adult heights in a family.
check.modelAnswer: The genes set a range of potential, and each member's diet and lifestyle during growth decide where within that range they land.

check.stem: A farmer feeds two groups of genetically similar chickens different diets. One group grows larger. Classify the size difference between the groups.
check.modelAnswer: The size difference is environmental, since the groups share similar genes and the diets altered how far each group's growth potential developed.

glossary.definition: Differences between individuals of the same species.
Traits falling into distinct classes, usually genetic and monogenic.
Traits spreading across a range, combining polygenic genes with environment.
Everything outside the organism that affects it, from diet to climate.
